base_text: You are setting the dining table for a holiday dinner. A relative walks into the room.

variants.warm: They pick up a stack of plates and offer to help you finish the table setup.
variants.cold: They walk past the table to look out the window without offering any assistance.
variants.adversarial: They say that the silverware is mismatched and the plates are laid out wrong.
variants.neutral: They take a seat at the far end of the table and begin reading their phone.

base_text: You are looking through an old photo album in the living room. Your sibling sits down.

variants.warm: They point at a picture and share a detailed story about that afternoon.
variants.cold: They flip on the television and stare at the screen without acknowledging the album.
variants.adversarial: They point at the pictures and say those events were completely exaggerated by everyone.
variants.neutral: They pull out a magazine from the coffee table and start reading it quietly.

base_text: You are cleaning up toys from the floor. A family member walks by the doorway.

variants.warm: They grab a handful of blocks and toss them into the storage bin for you.
variants.cold: They step carefully over the mess and continue down the hallway without stopping.
variants.adversarial: They kick a toy out of their way and mutter about the house being messy.
variants.neutral: They pause to let you pick up a piece near their foot, then keep walking.

base_text: You are telling a story about your day at the dinner table. Someone interrupts you.

variants.warm: They ask a thoughtful question that shows they are paying close attention to you.
variants.cold: They start a completely unrelated conversation with the person sitting next to them.
variants.adversarial: They roll their eyes and say they have heard this exact story before already.
variants.neutral: They ask someone to pass the salt shaker and then go back to eating.

base_text: You are struggling to carry a heavy box of decorations inside. A cousin is nearby.

variants.warm: They rush over to grab the other side of the box to share the heavy load.
variants.cold: They turn their back and pretend not to notice you struggling with the weight.
variants.adversarial: They cross their arms and say you should have carried fewer items at once.
variants.neutral: They hold the front door open for you until you make it all the way inside.
